findings.title: Ranger favored-enemy/favored-terrain/combat-style bonus-feat blocks are ~1400 lines of near-identical per-tier if-let arms
findings.evidence: explain_ranger_level1_chassis_and_class_feature_separation contains 5 near-identical combat-style bonus-feat blocks (34637-34897, one per tier 2/6/10/14/18), 5 near-identical favored-enemy selection+bonus blocks (34926-35505, one per interval 1/5/10/15/20), and 4 near-identical favored-terrain blocks (35607-36007, tiers 3/8/13/18). Each block repeats the same choice_selection -> match-to-restricted-name -> push ComputationExplanation shape, differing only in level thresholds, choice-id constants, and a hardcoded option list. E.g. lines 34702-34751 (2nd combat-style bonus feat) vs 34763-34812 (3rd) vs 34828-34854 (4th) are structurally identical modulo the swapped constant names.
findings.fix_description: Replace the per-tier arms with one table of (interval_level, choice_id, restricted_option_list_or_open_ended) tuples consumed by a single loop/helper, mirroring the pattern already used for barbarian_rage_tier/monk_unarmed_strike_damage_die elsewhere in the file. Would collapse ~1400 lines to well under 200 while keeping every id/detail string derivable from the tuple.
findings.risk_notes: Each explanation id and detail string is treated as a public contract read by v06_work_inventory's classifier (per in-file comments elsewhere in this chunk), so any refactor must preserve exact ids/values -- not mechanically provable by cargo check alone, needs a snapshot/receipt diff.

findings.title: generic_pool_group_selection_observed_keys recovers structured data by substring-scanning free-text explanation detail strings
findings.evidence: The function greps every ComputationExplanation.detail for the literal marker "corpus key `" and slices out the text up to the next backtick, to recover which corpus keys were genuinely emitted this run (used by v06_work_inventory's completion-atlas classifier per the doc comment at 41319-41340). The two emitting call sites' format strings live ~120 and ~940 lines away (push_generic_pool_choice_magnitude line ~41222, push_generic_pool_group_selection_magnitude line ~41304).
findings.fix_description: Carry the corpus key as a real struct field (or a side-channel Vec<String> returned alongside explanations) instead of parsing it back out of prose meant for humans; the doc comment already argues this was a deliberate choice to avoid reconstructing the id-slug scheme, but a typed field would remove the have-to-keep-two-format-strings-in-sync risk entirely.
findings.risk_notes: If either emitting format string's wording changes (e.g. someone rewords "corpus key" or changes the backtick quoting) this silently returns fewer keys with no compiler or type-level signal -- only a downstream count drift, which per repo history (see docs/release/SD-34 notes on 'field name is not its meaning') has previously been mistaken for a real regression rather than a string-format break.

findings.title: A third ComputationExplanation record duplicates an already-pushed value purely to satisfy a downstream classifier's suffix matching
findings.evidence: class_feature.ranger.favored_enemy (35250-35263) pushes the exact same favored_enemy_bonus value already pushed twice above under class_chassis.ranger.favored_enemy_skill_bonus (35206) and class_chassis.ranger.favored_enemy_attack_damage_bonus (35220), solely because v06_work_inventory.rs's CLASS_FEATURE_ID_MAGNITUDE_SUFFIXES list does not recognize the "_skill_bonus"/"_attack_damage_bonus"/"_choice" suffixes those two ids end in (per the comment's own admission).
findings.fix_description: Fix the classifier's suffix list (or its matching predicate) to recognize the two existing ids, removing the need for a third, value-duplicating explanation record whose only job is to be found by a naming convention.
findings.risk_notes: Out of this file's scope (fix lives in v06_work_inventory.rs / scripts/completion_atlas.py territory, both excluded from auto_fix by the review's own ground rules); flagging for correlation only.

findings.title: Redundant .expect() re-derives a value the enclosing if-condition already proved Some
findings.evidence: if recognized_bonus_feat_name == Some("Catch Off-Guard") || recognized_bonus_feat_name == Some("Throw Anything") { let feat_name = recognized_bonus_feat_name.expect("checked above"); ... }
findings.fix_description: Rewrite as `if let Some(feat_name @ ("Catch Off-Guard" | "Throw Anything")) = recognized_bonus_feat_name { ... }` to remove the panic-shaped call entirely; behaviorally identical today since the condition guarantees Some, so purely a clarity fix.
findings.risk_notes: No live risk -- the expect cannot actually panic given the guard -- purely a style/simplification note.
